name: Hawaii
summary: Hawaii has the highest electricity prices in the country and no ISO market, retail choice or capacity tags, so battery value comes from demand charges, utility programs and, for the few customers still on a time-of-use rate, arbitrage. On Oahu, Schedule J ($15.77/kW, under 300 kW) and Schedule P ($32.14/kW, 300 kW and up) bill demand as the higher of the month's peak or the mean of the current and highest prior-11-month peaks, with 25 kW and 300 kW minimums. Utility programs are the VPP route: Fast DR pays $5/kW-month for 50 kW or more on Oahu and Maui, and BYOD Plus pays $400/kW upfront for solar-charged batteries committed for five years. Hawaii Energy adds a $150 to $250 per kWh commercial storage rebate on Oahu and Maui. Commercial time-of-use rates are closed to new customers, the fuel charge swings between about 18 and 29 cents/kWh, and Schedule P customers do not get the non-export fast path. Values for Maui, Hawaii Island and KIUC are base-tariff or single-source figures and need bill confirmation.
default_energy_price_note: Approximate all-in commercial $/kWh (analyst assumption from the January to July 2026 Oahu fuel-charge range of 18 to 29 cents plus delivery; used only to cost round-trip losses). Enter the site's actual price.
data_notes: Researched 2026-10-05 from web-search summaries of Hawaiian Electric tariff sheets, effective-rate summaries, ECRC filings and program pages (direct document retrieval was blocked). Treat low-confidence values as screening estimates and enter bill rates in the Rate panel.

utilities.name: Hawaiian Electric (Oahu)
utilities.default_supply_notes: Vertically integrated: no retail choice and no capacity or transmission tags. Fuel and purchased-power costs are recovered through the monthly Energy Cost Recovery Clause (ECRC), a flat per-kWh charge on every hour for Schedules G, J, DS, P and F. Oahu ECRC was 18.449 cents/kWh in January 2026 and 27.285 cents/kWh in July 2026, so volumetric prices swing widely.
utilities.network_grid_notes: Downtown Honolulu and Chinatown are served by an underground network from Iwilei Substation (12 circuits). Network service restricts distributed generation, and microgrid interconnection to a spot or grid network is not allowed under the microgrid tariff. Expect non-export and extra review for batteries on the downtown network; the network boundary was not verified.

interconnection.rule_name: Hawaiian Electric Rule 14H (distributed generating facilities), Smart Renewable Energy Non-Export, and Rule 33 (BYOD)

tracks.name: Smart Renewable Energy Non-Export (expedited, Rule 14H Appendix III)
tracks.conditions: No export across the point of interconnection except grid support. Open to Schedule R, G and J customers (and TOU variants) only, so Schedule P customers are not eligible. Standalone storage has no stated capacity limit under the program (size governed by Rule 14H); a non-export facility with generation plus storage must be under 100 kW. Expedited review even in areas with voltage limitations.

tracks.name: Standard Rule 14H interconnection review
tracks.conditions: Distributed generating facilities that incorporate storage obtain an interconnection review under Rule 14H and meet the Company's interconnection standards. Larger, exporting or Schedule P facilities take this path.

interconnection.non_export_path: Non-export is the fast path (Smart Renewable Energy Non-Export), limited to Schedule R/G/J customers. The facility must be designed to minimize transfer to the utility and may not export except for grid support. Some summaries state that generators not interconnected with the distribution system, and facilities made up solely of storage, may not require a Rule 14H review; this was not confirmed for commercial standalone batteries, so confirm with the utility before relying on it.
interconnection.storage_specific_notes: BYOD Plus requires the battery to charge from renewable generation, so a grid-charged demand-shaving battery does not qualify. Grid-support functions (Smart DER, UL 1741-SB / IEEE 1547) are expected.

programs.status_notes: Open to commercial and industrial customers on Oahu and Maui County that can commit at least 50 kW. Hawaii Island was not listed.

eligibility.other: Utility pays for the enabling technology that automates curtailment. A battery that discharges to hold the site's load down during an event counts as load reduction at the meter.

site_constraints.title: Honolulu Fire Code is based on NFPA 1 (2021 edition)
site_constraints.rule: The City and County of Honolulu Fire Code is based on NFPA 1, 2021 edition, whose Chapter 52 covers stationary energy storage systems. HFD requires permits and plan review. Residential storage is capped at 20 kWh per dwelling unit and UL 9540A data is needed to exceed it. Behind-the-meter systems in commercial or multi-family buildings may use a professional self-certification pathway. The model thresholds in the federal rules (20 kWh permit, 50 kWh unit, 600 kWh group, setbacks) are applied as the baseline.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Plan on the model-code limits: outdoor group limits and setbacks drive unit count and placement. Confirm the exact NFPA 855 edition and any Honolulu amendments with HFD, and the county for sites off Oahu.
site_constraints.applies_to: Honolulu (Oahu). Other counties adopt their own fire codes.

site_constraints.title: Hawaii adopts the 2023 NEC; Honolulu's local edition may lag
site_constraints.rule: The Hawaii State Building Code Council adopted the 2023 NEC (NFPA 70) statewide, effective September 1 2024 per a secondary source. County adoption can lag by up to two years, so Honolulu may still enforce an older edition. NEC 705.12 (120% rule) and Article 706 apply in all recent editions.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Use the NEC 120% backfeed rule (checked by the tool) and confirm the edition with the permitting office.

site_constraints.title: Smart Renewable Energy Non-Export covers Schedule R/G/J only
site_constraints.rule: The expedited non-export path (Rule 14H Appendix III) is open to Schedule R, G and J customers and their TOU variants. Schedule P customers go through the standard Rule 14H review. A non-export facility made up of generation plus storage must be under 100 kW (sum of inverter string capacities); standalone storage has no stated capacity limit under the program. The facility may not export except for grid support.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: A battery at a Schedule J site (under 300 kW) can use the fast path; a Schedule P site (300 kW or more) should plan for a longer standard review. Keep PV-plus-storage under 100 kW on the fast path.

site_constraints.title: Coastal, flood and hurricane siting
site_constraints.rule: Many Hawaii commercial sites are near the shoreline. Expect scrutiny of FEMA flood and tsunami zones, Special Management Area review near the coast, hurricane wind loads and salt-air corrosion (outdoor enclosures rated for corrosive environments). Practitioner knowledge, not a verified code threshold.
site_constraints.impact_on_sizing: Can limit ground-level placement and push batteries to elevated pads or indoor rooms (which then fall under the indoor limits). Check the flood-zone box in the screener.

sources.title: City and County of Honolulu Fire Code based on NFPA 1 (2021 edition)

panel_notes.topic: Billing demand averages in the prior 11 months
panel_notes.note: On Schedules J and P, billing demand is the greater of the month's peak or the mean of the current peak and the highest peak of the previous 11 months. Shaving one month does little; the battery has to hold every month's peak so the highest prior month comes down too. Schedule P also bills at least 300 kW, so a site peaking near 300 kW saves almost nothing.

panel_notes.topic: Fuel charge swings dwarf demand charges
panel_notes.note: The Oahu ECRC moved from 18.4 cents/kWh in January 2026 to about 29 cents in June and 27.3 cents in July. The charge applies to every kWh, so it raises the cost of round-trip losses but not the spread. Demand charges ($15.77 on Schedule J, $32.14 on Schedule P) are the stable part of the value.

Schedule TOU-J is closed to new customers and the Shift and Save / ARD commercial TOU closed to new enrollments on Feb 1 2025. A new commercial site is on a flat energy price (Schedule J or P), so arbitrage value is limited to existing TOU customers.

Hawaiian Electric has proposed a rebasing increase of about $170 million a year ($125 million from January 2027, $45 million from January 2028) in Docket 2026-0162. Demand-charge values may rise if approved.

panel_notes.topic: Fast path is for Schedule J, not P
panel_notes.note: Smart Renewable Energy Non-Export fast-tracks Schedule R/G/J customers only. A 200 kW battery at a Schedule P site (300 kW or more) takes the standard Rule 14H review, so start the application early. PV plus storage on the fast path must stay under 100 kW.

BYOD Plus pays $400/kW but the battery must charge from renewable generation and be committed for five years. If the business plan is grid-charged demand shaving, the incentive does not apply; if there is rooftop PV, compare the two designs.

Honolulu's fire code is based on NFPA 1, 2021 edition. Commercial behind-the-meter systems may qualify for professional self-certification, but outdoor group limits and setbacks still drive layout. Add flood, tsunami and salt-air checks on coastal sites.

Hawaii has no retail choice and no ISO market, so a third-party aggregator cannot sell capacity or ancillary services the way it can on the mainland. The VPP revenue available today is utility-run: Fast DR ($5/kW-month) and BYOD Plus ($400/kW).

open_questions: Current effective Schedule J and P demand charges: the $15.77 and $32.14 figures come from search summaries of the January 2026 effective-rate summaries. Confirm on a recent bill, and whether the May 2026 filing changed them.

Whether the January 2026 base-rate adjustment (about 1.213x on customer and demand charges) also scales the TOU energy charges. If it does, the TOU-J on-peak vs mid-day spread is about 9.7 cents instead of 8.0 cents.

Oahu Schedule TOU-P, Schedule U (optional TOU demand rate: $30.50 priority-peak and $27.50 mid-peak base) and Schedule DS: rates and whether they are open to new customers were not verified, so they are not modeled.
Maui Schedule P and Hawaii Island Schedule J: rates not found. Maui Schedule J and Hawaii Island Schedule P are base tariff-sheet values and are probably about 20% below today's effective charges.
KIUC: only Schedule LP (May 2025 sheet) was found; 2026 rates after the rate case, KIUC's TOU options, and any customer battery or demand-response program were not found.

BYOD Plus: maximum committed kW for a commercial site, whether a non-export site qualifies, and whether it can be combined with Fast DR on the same battery.
Whether a standalone, non-exporting commercial battery needs a Rule 14H review at all (some summaries say storage-only facilities do not); confirm with Hawaiian Electric before relying on it.
Hawaii State Fire Council / county adoption of NFPA 855 and the NEC edition Honolulu enforces; Maui, Hawaii and Kauai county fire codes were not researched.
